messages:
customer_acme_ops: Hey @simon — we flipped a staged model rollout around 02:00 UTC (v4.2 -> v4.3) and started getting structured-output parse failures on our order webhook. Parsers now choke because some objects are coming back wrapped as {\"value\": null} instead of being omitted or plain objects. This is breaking our webhook consumer. Samples attached. :frowning:

simon: Sorry to hear that — can you paste an exact failing response and the request you sent? Which API route / model name / structured_output flags are you using? Any streaming enabled?

customer_acme_ops: Minimal failing response (sanitized):
```json
{
  "order_id": "ord_123",
  "customer": {"value": null},
  "items": [{"id": "sku_1", "qty": 2}],
  "meta": {"notes": {"value": null}}
}
```
Request we send: POST /v1/responses with body:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-v4.3",
  "input": "Generate structured order JSON for order ord_123 with optional customer and notes",
  "structured_output": true
}
```
We were previously on redwood-v4.2 and didn't see the null wrappers. Also noticed token counts spiked on the next billing cycle.

ingrid: @customer_acme_ops thanks — very helpful. Quick hypothesis: v4.3 introduced a small change in the structured-output postprocessor where optional absent objects are serialized as {\"value\": null} to preserve explicit null semantics for downstream evals. That would explain the wrapping. Did you pin a model variant previously (e.g., redwood-v4.2:stable) or were you following alias \"redwood-latest\"?

customer_acme_ops: We followed "redwood-latest" (no pin). We have a pin for production but this was a staging test. Any quick mitigation? Parsers are brittle.

anya: For immediate mitigation you can set structured_output_config to prefer_omit_nulls: true or use the compatibility flag legacy_null_handling=true in the request. Example curl we use for compatibility:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model":"redwood-v4.3",
    "input":"Generate structured order JSON...",
    "structured_output": true,
    "structured_output_config": {"prefer_omit_nulls": true}
  }'
```
This should return omitted keys rather than null-wrapped.

simon: Can you try that and paste results? If that works we'll escalate a permanent fix or a migration doc. Also, can you share the route you hit and the request-id headers from a failing call? That helps trace on the runtime.

customer_acme_ops: Tried prefer_omit_nulls and it does fix the wrapper on staging. Repro steps we recorded:
1) Use alias redwood-latest (which routed to v4.3 after staged rollout)
2) POST as above with structured_output=true and no structured_output_config
3) Observe wrapped nulls in customer and meta.notes
We grabbed request-ids: req_01H9AB2C3, req_01H9AB2C7, req_01H9AB2D0. Logs attached.

ingrid: Thanks — we'll pull logs for those request-ids. Early notes for the incident ticket: probable intentional behavior change to preserve explicit nulls; side-effect is increased tokenization cost because wrapper keys are emitted. That matches your billing spike. We'll check whether alias routing should have warned about the schema change.

customer_acme_ops: Two asks: 1) a short-term toggle in the hosted API to re-enable legacy null omission by alias so we can avoid pinning; 2) documentation/notice when model variants introduce structured-output format changes.

anya: For 1) we've got the compatibility flag already; we can add a per-alias compatibility toggle but it'll require an infra change. I'll open an internal request. For 2) agree — we should add a breaking-change note in release notes and the model catalog page.

dev-support-bot: Ticket created: REDWOOD-SUP-5423 by anya — assigned to eng-ml. Linked requests: req_01H9AB2C3, req_01H9AB2C7, req_01H9AB2D0.

simon: Next steps for us: eng-ml (ingrid) will confirm whether v4.3 behavior is intentional, add migration guidance to the model catalog if so, and ops will evaluate per-alias compatibility toggle. I'll keep you updated here. Thanks for the quick repro and request-ids. :thumbsup:

customer_acme_ops: Appreciated. We'll pin production to redwood-v4.2 for now and enable the compatibility flag in staging. Keep us posted.

anya: FYI — if anyone else in #support sees more of these, reply with request-ids and whether the compatibility flag fixed it.

ingrid: Logged initial findings in REDWOOD-SUP-5423: v4.3 introduced explicit-null serialization for structured_output to support downstream nullable type validation. Engineering to propose either a global compatibility toggle or revert for alias-based rollout.

simon: Closing loop: customer pinned prod, staging uses compatibility flag, ticket open. Follow-ups: release notes update, alias-toggle eval, and a small cost-impact note for customers.

customer_acme_ops: Thanks all. This helped a lot.
